request.spec:
A steward can undo the last merge into a person on the same sheet-today it was made (a button on
the row; PERSON_MERGE_UNDONE name=<the person restored> from=<the person merged into>): the merged
person is back at the end of the list with the claims that came from them (their numbers and
status as they are now) and their own aliases, which leave the other's; patron and pool changes
stay. Any later day, anyone else, or a person with no merge to undo is refused with an error.

agent.result_text:
Undoing a merge now works: there's an **Undo merge** button on each person's row. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests (the merge-undo test and the three scenario tests).

**What an undo does**
- The merged person comes back with the same id, at the end of the list. Their grades, holds, watchers, approver, retirement and terms come back as they were just before the merge.
- The claims that came from them go back to them as they are now (numbers and status). This only applies to claims still under the person they were merged into.
- Their own aliases move back off the other person, and the alias their name had become is removed.
- Patron and pool changes stay, as asked. Statements, period totals and crew changes from the merge also stay.
- The audit file gets `PERSON_MERGE_UNDONE sheet=… by=… name=<restored> from=<merged into>`, then the usual ROLLUP and TOTALS lines.

**When it's refused** (shows `person-error`, writes nothing)
- The user isn't a steward, or isn't the user who made the merge. I read "anyone else" as anyone other than whoever made the merge.
- It's no longer the sheet-today the merge was made.
- The person has no merge into them, or their most recent merge has already been undone. Only the most recent merge can be undone, so an older merge can't be undone after the newer one is.
- Someone else on the sheet now has the merged person's name. I added this check myself so the undo can't fail halfway.

**How it's built**
- **Migration** `V111__person_merge_undo.sql`: a table recording each merge, plus copies of the rows a merge deletes. The copy tables mirror the existing ones and are filled and restored without listing columns by hand. If a later migration adds a column to `person` (or another copied table), the copy table needs the same column, or that column won't be restored.
- **Merge change**: `PersonMerger.merge` now saves this record before it deletes anything, so merges made before this change can't be undone.
- **Code**: the new `MergeUndoer` repository does the saving and restoring. The new endpoint `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/merge-undo` has its validate, check, rollup, undo, audit and respond steps in `person/`. The button is in `features/merge/merge.slot.tsx` (`data-testid="person-merge-undo"`).
